-- ACID Properties in DBMS Explanation:
-- 1. Atomicity: Either all operations in a transaction succeed, or all roll back via undo logging.
-- 2. Consistency: Database transitions strictly between valid schema integrity constraints.
-- 3. Isolation: Transactions execute without dirty read / non-repeatable read interference.
-- 4. Durability: Committed data survives crashes via Write-Ahead Logging (WAL) flushed to non-volatile disk.

comments.text: Good use of prefix sums! What happens if the array contains negative numbers? Note that storing only the first occurrence keeps the longest length, which is correct.
Excellent O(N) time and O(N) space solution. Clean single-pass hash map approach. Approved!
Watch out for integer overflow: when low and high are both large, `(low + high)` can exceed Integer.MAX_VALUE. Please revise using `low + (high - low) / 2` and resubmit.
